messages:
alex: Customer report — 3rd-party payment webhook triggered twice when using our function_call tool. They see duplicate charges. Repro steps and payload below, can someone help triage?

chris: ack, can you paste the request + response logs? especially the tool call payload and the runtime response codes.

alex: pasted logs:
```
Request -> POST /v1/generate
body: { model: \"redwood-chat-1\", input: \"charge user\", function_call: { name: \"payment_webhook\", args: { amount: 100, user_id: \"u-123\" } } }
```
Runtime log for tool invocation: 
```
[2026-02-25T14:02:12Z] tool-invoke id=ti-899 status=202 body=\"accepted for processing\"
[2026-02-25T14:02:13Z] retry-scheduler id=ti-899 reason=no-terminal-response retry=1
[2026-02-25T14:02:13Z] tool-invoke id=ti-899 status=200 body=\"ok webhook sent\"
```
Customer says their payment provider processed two charges 1s apart.

priya: interesting — runtime returned a 202 then a 200 after a retry. Do we have client-side or platform retries for tool invocations when initial response is non-2xx?

eng-ml: yes, platform has a short retry backoff for tool adapters in cases where the tool returns a non-terminal status like 202/204 without a clear completion. The intention was to handle async adapters, but this can double-execute external side effects if the adapter doesn't support idempotency.

alex: customer is irate — they were charged twice and want refund. Also asking why our SDK apparently retried and caused this.

chris: steps I'm taking: 1) confirm platform retry policy for tools (time window, max attempts); 2) ask payment provider if they accept idempotency keys or have dedupe; 3) suggest immediate mitigation to customer.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-57 - duplicate external webhook execution. Assigned: @sara.

sara: I pulled the adapter logs. The webhook adapter returned 202 because it queued a job, then the job processor completed ~900ms later and adapter emitted a 200. Our retry logic saw the initial 202 and scheduled one retry within 1s. Because the adapter didn't surface a stable idempotency token, both calls resulted in two deliveries.

priya: Can we reproduce locally with a simple mock that returns 202 then 200? I can run a quick harness.

eng-ml: repro is trivial. Example harness:
```
# mock server pseudocode
POST /webhook -> if first_call then return 202; queue job that sends payment; on next poll return 200
```
Run conversation through SDK with function_call. We'll see two tool invokes in logs.

chris: Is the duplicate charge a billing platform charge (our customer billed by us) or an external merchant charge (their payment provider billing end users)? Customer indicates external provider charged twice. They now want us to provide evidence and coordinate refund. @billing can you advise?

billing: we don't bill for the webhook delivery itself (customers pay for tokens/calls) but we need to help customer with evidence to the payment provider for refund. We can export request ids, timestamps, and the two delivery payloads. I'll prepare that CSV.

alex: immediate workaround suggested to customer: set function_call to not retry in the SDK by passing retry:false and to make the adapter return a clear 409/200 on duplicate attempts, or add an idempotency header from the caller (we can suggest X-Idempotency-Key generated per user action). They asked if we can patch runtime to avoid retrying when adapter returns 202 — can we do that quickly?

eng-ml: short-term mitigation: change retry policy to treat 202 as terminal for tool adapters that declare themselves "async-accepted" via adapter metadata. That requires a small runtime flag update. Medium-term: require adapters that can do side effects to accept idempotency tokens (recommended).

priya: I opened a hotfix branch that respects adapter metadata key `accepts_async_ack` — if true, do not auto-retry on 202, instead emit a guidance event in the console. Patch diff: 
```
- if (status === 202) scheduleRetry()
+ if (status === 202 && !adapter.accepts_async_ack) scheduleRetry()
```
Will run canary in staging.

chris: good. For the customer, propose three actions: 1) Refund request to external payment provider (we'll attach logs), 2) Ask them to add idempotency key to payload, 3) We deploy hotfix to stop automatic retry for async-accept adapters.

alex: customer also asked whether they were billed extra by us for the retry. They saw only one usage spike (tokens for generation) but not sure about tool-call billing.

billing: tool-call billing shows one recorded tool invocation (we bill on final status). We'll confirm but I think we didn't double-bill for tool execution.

ops-bot: Canaries started: staging -> 5% traffic for runtime flag change.

sara: notes for postmortem: root cause = platform retry semantics + async-accepted 202 responses from adapter lacking idempotency. Impact = duplicate external side-effects (external charges). Mitigation = runtime change + adapter idempotency requirement + user guidance.

chris: customer facing note drafted: short apology + explanation + attached logs + recommended config change (X-Idempotency-Key) + timeframe for runtime fix (ETA 2 business days). Alex, can you send to customer once I add logs?

alex: will send now. Thanks all.

eng-ml: follow-ups: add telemetry to count tool invocations with initial non-200 then retry, and surface in console warnings for adapters that signal async acceptance; long-term: add an adapter-level contract requiring idempotency support or return of a canonical operation id.

billing: CSV with timestamps and payloads attached to the incident.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-57 status -> monitoring (severity: high).

sara: closing loop: staging canary looks good, no regressions. Rolling to prod in 3h with feature-flag toggle. Will link rollout PR in the incident.

chris: thanks everyone. If this recurs after prod roll, escalate to oncall immediately. :thumbsup:
